gloss: scrap of paper; slip of paper

definitions.gloss: scrap of paper; slip of paper; paper fragment
definitions.explanation: A small piece or fragment of paper, often torn or cut from a larger sheet. Used in literary and formal contexts to describe notes, messages, or remnants of paper.

examples.japanese: {紙片|しへん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{落|お}ちていた→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧。
examples.english: A scrap of paper had fallen on the ground.

examples.japanese: ⟦ポケット→ポケット：02964_poketto⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{小|ちい}さな→小さな：02913_chiisana⟧{紙片|しへん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}り{出|だ}した→取り出す：04220_toridasu⟧。
examples.english: I took out a small slip of paper from my pocket.

examples.japanese: ⟦{床|ゆか}→床：03652_yuka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{散|ち}らばった→散らばる：12713_chirabaru⟧{紙片|しへん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{一枚一枚|いちまいいちまい}{拾|ひろ}い{集|あつ}めた。
examples.english: I picked up the scraps of paper scattered on the floor one by one.

notes:
A somewhat literary or formal word for a small piece of paper. In everyday conversation, ⟦{紙切|かみき}れ→紙切れ：22090_kamikire⟧ is more common, but {紙片|しへん} appears frequently in novels, news reports, and formal writing. Often implies something found, discovered, or left behind — a note slipped under a door, a torn fragment at a crime scene, or a scribbled message.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紙片|しへん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{拾|ひろ}う→拾う：00845_hirou⟧: to pick up a scrap of paper
- {紙片|しへん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧: to write on a slip of paper
- ⟦{小|ちい}さな→小さな：02913_chiisana⟧{紙片|しへん}: a small scrap of paper
- ⟦{一枚|いちまい}→一枚：08889_ichimai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{紙片|しへん}: a single slip of paper

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{紙切|かみき}れ→紙切れ：22090_kamikire⟧: scrap of paper — everyday equivalent; more colloquial
- ⟦メモ→メモ：00274_memo⟧: memo, note — focuses on the content written rather than the physical paper
- ⟦{断片|だんぺん}→断片：10915_danpen⟧: fragment — more general; used for any broken piece, not just paper
